# Prerequisites {#sec-prerequisites} ## Installing Julia {#sec-installing} Use **`juliaup`**, the official version manager. Do not install Julia through a system package manager (`apt`, `brew`), which tends to ship outdated versions. ::: {.panel-tabset} ## macOS and Linux ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh ``` ## Windows ```powershell winget install julia -s msstore ``` ::: Afterwards, `juliaup update` upgrades and `juliaup status` lists installed versions. ## Project environments {#sec-environments} This is the most important concept in the chapter, and the one that differs most from common practice in R. In R, `install.packages()` installs into a global library shared by all your projects. In Julia, each project has its own environment, described by two files: - **`Project.toml`** — the direct dependencies you declared. - **`Manifest.toml`** — the full resolved dependency tree, with exact versions of everything. Together they make an analysis reproducible by construction: anyone who clones your repository and runs `Pkg.instantiate()` gets exactly your versions. ::: {.r-equivalent} **In R** `Project.toml` + `Manifest.toml` play the role of `renv.lock`, but they are part of the language rather than an add-on package. Activating an environment is the default operation, not the exception. ::: ::: {#env-status .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Pkg Pkg.status() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ## This book's environment {#sec-book-environment} ::: {#versioninfo .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} versioninfo() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Julia Version 1.12.6 Commit 15346901f00 (2026-04-09 19:20 UTC) Build Info: Official https://julialang.org release Platform Info: OS: macOS (arm64-apple-darwin24.0.0) CPU: 10 × Apple M5 WORD_SIZE: 64 LLVM: libLLVM-18.1.7 (ORCJIT, apple-m1) GC: Built with stock GC Threads: 1 default, 1 interactive, 1 GC (on 4 virtual cores) Environment: JULIA_LOAD_PATH = @:@stdlib ``` ::: ::: To reproduce the book: ```bash git clone cd EcologicalAnalysesInJulia julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()' ``` ## Editor {#sec-editor} **VS Code** with the official language extension is the standard recommendation: it offers an integrated REPL, variable inspector, debugger and line-by-line evaluation (`Shift+Enter`) — the functional equivalent of RStudio. Alternatives: **Pluto.jl** (reactive notebooks, excellent for teaching) and any editor with LSP support through `LanguageServer.jl`. ## Quarto {#sec-quarto} This book is written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org), the direct successor to `bookdown`. Since version 1.5, Quarto executes Julia blocks natively, without going through Jupyter. ````markdown ```{{julia}} #| label: example 1 + 1 ``` ```` ## Exercises {.unnumbered} 1.
